meta.note: Detail dressing for Tokyo (same frame as tokyo_layout.json). trains: ONE clean ordered polyline per line, clipped to the play box, north / Shimbashi end first: {name, kind: yamanote | shinkansen | monorail | yurikamome, points, elevated, deckMetres (typical deck height above the street), stops (in line order, names from OSM), lengthU}. rail: the other mapped surface / elevated tracks as raw polylines (the Tokaido, Yokosuka, Keihin-Tohoku and Keikyu lines, the Shinkansen approaches, the Yurikamome and monorail second tracks); elevated = on a bridge or viaduct; subways and tunnels are left out. ferries: real routes from OSM, first point at the dock inside the box, clipped at the fetch area: the Sumida River water buses from Hinode Pier and Hama-rikyu up-river toward Asakusa and across to Odaiba, the Harumi boat, and the island ships from Takeshiba that sail out of the bay past the bounds. piers: the deck polygons of tokyo_layout parks with surface 'pier'. seawall: the quay line (the land edge with jetties under 50 m wide removed), polylines. rainbowBridge: see its note. expressways: the elevated Shuto Expressway / Tokyo Expressway decks as clean polylines, one carriageway of each pair ({name, points, deckMetres}); the level may draw decks on pylons along them. containerShip: {x, z, rot}. skytree: the true position, for the note.
meta.expresswayNote: expressways: the Shuto Expressway pieces OSM tags as bridges (no tunnels, no sunken or at-grade pieces), both carriageways, chained, each {layer, deckMetres, points, lengthU}; deckMetres from the OSM layer. tools/tokyo/cartographer/refine_expressways.py

trains.name: JR Yamanote Line
trains.note: the Yamanote loop / Keihin-Tohoku corridor on its 1910 red-brick arch viaduct from Tokyo Station through Yurakucho and Shimbashi, then on embankment and bridges past Hamamatsucho, Tamachi and Takanawa Gateway to Shinagawa at the south edge (one track of the mapped pair)

trains.name: Tokaido Shinkansen
trains.note: the Tokaido Shinkansen from its Tokyo Station platforms south beside the Yamanote viaduct through Yurakucho, Shimbashi and Hamamatsucho to the south edge (toward Shinagawa)

trains.name: Tokyo Monorail
trains.note: the Tokyo Monorail (straddle-beam, 1964) from Monorail Hamamatsucho station south over the Shibaura canals and along the Keihin canal toward Haneda

trains.name: Yurikamome
trains.note: the Yurikamome automated guideway from Shimbashi through Shiodome, Takeshiba, Hinode and Shibaura-futo, round the 270-degree loop and over the Rainbow Bridge (lower deck, about 50 m up) to Odaiba-kaihinkoen and Daiba, leaving the box toward Aomi and Toyosu

loop.note: the 270-degree loop of the lower-deck road and the Yurikamome on the Shibaura side (centre approximate; the Yurikamome line in trains follows it exactly)

rainbowBridge.note: Rainbow Bridge (1993): white three-span suspension bridge, 126 m towers, double deck (Shuto Expressway Route 11 above; the bay road, the Yurikamome and walkways below). points = the expressway deck centreline: the Shibaura approach viaduct from the north, the main bridge anchorage to anchorage and the Odaiba approach viaduct to the east edge of the box. x / z = mid-span of the OSM deck, rot = rotation.y with the deck along local +X (Shibaura to Odaiba); mainSpan = the two anchorage points 798 m apart; towers 285 m either side of mid-span by the published spans; heights above the water.

containerShip.note: a container ship at anchor in the port basin between the Toyosu wharf, Odaiba and the Rainbow Bridge (the fairway to the Harumi and Shibaura piers), inside the box

skytree.note: the true position of Tokyo Skytree at Oshiage (north-east, outside the box); in play it is moved to Harumi Futo Park (movedTo, the tokyo_skytree landmark)
